questions.q: Fix: 'I'm writing coz the streetlight hasn't worked for like two weeks and it's super annoying.'
questions.a: 'I am writing to report that the streetlight near my residence has been non-functional for two weeks.' A wrong answer fixing only the contraction leaves emotive residue ('very annoying') — every marker must convert.

questions.q: Is 'do the needful' good formal register?
questions.a: No — it is a dated Indianism boards mark down; say what is actually needed ('arrange daily collection'). A wrong answer shows the student mistakes officialese for formality.

questions.q: Which request close earns the mark: 'Fix this fast!!!' or 'I would be grateful if you could look into the matter at the earliest'?
questions.a: The second — courteous indirection carries the command in formal register. The first performs urgency instead of requesting action.

questions.q: Formal register bans ______, slang, exclamations, vague words (stuff, a lot, really), and emotional statements — it converts feelings into facts: 'smells gross' → 'poses a health hazard'.

Fill in the blank: Formal register bans ______, slang, exclamations, vague words (stuff, a lot, really), and emotional statements — it converts feelings into facts: 'smells gross' → 'poses a health hazard'.

Fill in the blank: The banned list hunt: ______ (can't→cannot), slang (gross→unhygienic), intensifiers (really bad→a matter of serious concern), exclamations (delete), vagueness (stuff→specific noun).
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student rewrites informal markers into formal equivalents, maintains third-person objectivity in complaint bodies, and closes requests with courteous fixed phrases.
